literal: Those who do penance do their own duty; others who do not, having fallen within desire, do ruin.
translation: Those who perform penance are the ones who truly perform their own duty; all others, caught in the grip of desire, only bring about their own ruin.
modern: தவம் செய்கின்றவர்களே தங்களுக்குரிய கடமையைச் செய்கின்றவர்கள் ஆவர்; அவ்வாறு செய்யாத மற்றவர்கள் ஆசையில் சிக்கித் தங்களுக்குக் கேடு விளைவித்துக் கொள்கிறார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet defines the true nature of duty and action. It states that those who practice penance (tavam) are the only ones who are actually performing their true duty (karumam), as they master themselves. On the other hand, those who do not practice penance are trapped by worldly desires (ācai) and end up doing things that lead to waste or ruin (avam). The contrast between 'karumam' (meaningful duty/action) and 'avam' (wasteful/harmful action) highlights that self-control is essential for any meaningful life endeavor.
